policy.purpose: Choose mathematical and conceptual machinery by the proof role it controls.
rejection_rules: Reject machinery that names a field without a controlled interface.
Reject endpoint language used as construction machinery.
Reject proxy evidence used as proof authority without transfer certification.
Reject witness machinery before the target object and representation are available.

roles.construction: Builds the target object or a regulated approximation that can be transferred to it.
roles.invariant_preservation: Keeps essential commitments unchanged across transformations.
roles.obstruction: Explains why a naive route fails and what must be repaired.
roles.representation: Gives the target object a tractable mathematical form.
roles.transfer: Moves information between regimes, formalisms, limits, or reconstructed objects.
roles.validation: Checks that the route proves the intended target rather than a nearby proxy.
roles.witness: Produces a detectable property that would certify the target claim.

policy.title: Abstraction And Machinery Selection Policy

assumptions_required: regulated compact simple gauge-field objects are defined
uniform multiscale estimates are available
reflection positivity or a route to OS positivity is preserved
selections.controlled_interface: regulated gauge-field measures or effective actions -> continuum Schwinger-function object
selections.example_alignment: Yang-Mills: Balaban-style RG is construction machinery for the continuum object, not the final gap witness.
invalid_use_modes: Treating finite-volume or small-field RG control as continuum construction.
Counting ultraviolet stability as an infrared mass gap.
Losing gauge invariance or OS positivity in the limit.
selections.machinery_needed_because: The target cannot be reached by a spectral endpoint until a same-theory continuum object exists.
selections.machinery_not_yet_allowed: Do not use RG control itself as a mass-gap proof without a same-theory spectral witness.
selections.output_obligation: Produce a continuum Yang-Mills Schwinger-function family with nontrivial gauge-invariant observables.
selections.required_bridge_obligation: RG-to-OS bridge lemma with topology, limiting objects, positivity preservation, and nontriviality witness.

acceptable_weakenings: Euclidean OS-first construction is acceptable only when reconstruction, nontriviality, continuum limit, and positive mass-gap obligations remain explicit.
Regulated or lattice formulations are acceptable only as source objects for a certified continuum-transfer bridge.
forbidden_nearby_problems: A fixed-lattice or finite-volume mass gap without cutoff-removal transfer.
A lower-dimensional or scalar proxy theory without a same-target transfer theorem.
A perturbative ultraviolet statement treated as nonperturbative construction.
Numerical glueball or lattice spectroscopy evidence used as theorem authority.
A Hamiltonian spectral statement whose Hilbert space, vacuum, or observable algebra is postulated rather than reconstructed.
target_contract_summary.success_condition: Construct the continuum Yang-Mills theory and prove Delta > 0 for the reconstructed Hamiltonian in the same nontrivial compact-simple-gauge theory.

selections.target_object_link: A nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 for a compact simple gauge group G, satisfying OS/Wightman adequacy and a strictly positive Hamiltonian mass gap in the reconstructed physical theory.
selections.why_best_available: The active obstruction is construction and cutoff removal; RG directly controls scale dependence rather than postulating the continuum object.
selections.why_this_is_the_bottleneck: Scale control must become OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions before any spectral claim belongs to the target theory.

assumptions_required: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions exist
observables are gauge invariant and spectrally determining
decay constants remain bounded below during cutoff removal
selections.controlled_interface: gauge-invariant Euclidean time correlations -> Hamiltonian spectral support away from zero
selections.example_alignment: Yang-Mills: correlator decay is witness machinery for the gap, conditional on OS reconstruction and same-theory transfer.
invalid_use_modes: Using observables that do not generate the physical excitation sector.
Allowing decay constants to vanish under cutoff removal.
Separating the decay estimate from the reconstructed continuum theory.
selections.machinery_needed_because: The target requires a positive lower spectral threshold, not only existence of the theory.
selections.machinery_not_yet_allowed: Do not treat fixed-lattice or strong-coupling decay as a continuum gap proof.
selections.output_obligation: Prove support of relevant spectral measures is bounded away from zero.
selections.required_bridge_obligation: Decay-to-gap lemma with OS reconstruction, observable density, and cutoff-uniform constants.

selections.why_this_is_the_bottleneck: A decay estimate is meaningful for the Clay target only if constants and observables survive continuum reconstruction.

assumptions_required: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions exist
observables are gauge invariant and spectrally determining
decay constants remain bounded below during cutoff removal
selections.controlled_interface: gauge-invariant Euclidean time correlations -> Hamiltonian spectral support away from zero
selections.example_alignment: Yang-Mills: correlator decay is witness machinery for the gap, conditional on OS reconstruction and same-theory transfer.
invalid_use_modes: Using observables that do not generate the physical excitation sector.
Allowing decay constants to vanish under cutoff removal.
Separating the decay estimate from the reconstructed continuum theory.
selections.machinery_needed_because: The target requires a positive lower spectral threshold, not only existence of the theory.
selections.machinery_not_yet_allowed: Do not treat fixed-lattice or strong-coupling decay as a continuum gap proof.
selections.output_obligation: Prove support of relevant spectral measures is bounded away from zero.
selections.required_bridge_obligation: Decay-to-gap lemma with OS reconstruction, observable density, and cutoff-uniform constants.
selections.selected_machinery: Euclidean correlator decay and spectral-measure analysis

acceptable_weakenings: Euclidean OS-first construction is acceptable only when reconstruction, nontriviality, continuum limit, and positive mass-gap obligations remain explicit.
Regulated or lattice formulations are acceptable only as source objects for a certified continuum-transfer bridge.
forbidden_nearby_problems: A fixed-lattice or finite-volume mass gap without cutoff-removal transfer.
A lower-dimensional or scalar proxy theory without a same-target transfer theorem.
A perturbative ultraviolet statement treated as nonperturbative construction.
Numerical glueball or lattice spectroscopy evidence used as theorem authority.
A Hamiltonian spectral statement whose Hilbert space, vacuum, or observable algebra is postulated rather than reconstructed.
target_contract_summary.success_condition: Construct the continuum Yang-Mills theory and prove Delta > 0 for the reconstructed Hamiltonian in the same nontrivial compact-simple-gauge theory.
